stories.title: Oil-rich Alberta votes on Canada breakup
summary: Alberta decides Monday if it wants to pursue a binding referendum on leaving Canada, with Prime Minister Mark Carney warning a separatist win would bring dangerous uncertainty during a trade war with the United States.

After a separatist party won Quebec’s provincial election on October 5, tech billionaire Elon Musk posted that “they would be better off” if they seceded. “Alberta and Saskatchewan should separate too,” he added.

Development Council members from Khyber express ignorance about their role Meanwhile, Ittehad-i-Malkanan Bajaur, an alliance of elders, on Sunday rejected the ARDC, saying the alliance wasn’t consulted on the council’s formation.

The five members selected from Khyber also expressed their lack of knowledge about the selection criteria for council members, with some of the local elders declining the offer when they were approached by the district administration.

stories.title: Army major martyred, 4 terrorists killed in Balochistan IBOs: ISPR
summary: In the first operation on October 18, security forces conducted an IBO in the general area of Jattakabad, during which four terrorists were eliminated. “A large cache of arms and ammunition was also recovered,” it added.
In the second incident, ISPR added that security forces conducted a series of clearance operations in the general area of Shadi Kaur, Pasni, in Gwadar.
A day earlier, security forces killed eight “India-sponsored” terrorists during IBO conducted in the Quetta, Nushki and Khuzdar districts of Balochistan.

stories.title: Four terrorists held, hideouts destroyed in KP's Lakki operation
summary: LAKKI MARWAT: Four terrorists were arrested, and their hideouts were destroyed during a search and strike operation in Lakki Marwat district on Sunday.

stories.title: Climate-smart farming for rice growers to reduce water use discussed in Gujranwala consultation
summary: LAHORE: In a bid to slash agricultural water consumption by nearly a third and cut methane emissions almost by half, the rice sector is moving to adopt climate-smart farming techniques that can allow local growers to unlock lucrative international carbon markets.

At the core of the proposed transformation is the alternate wetting and drying (AWD), a precise water-management method where rice fields undergo controlled periods of drying rather than continuous flooding.

stories.title: Livestock card scheme behind 43pc rise in animal exports, claims Punjab govt
summary: LAHORE: Punjab’s livestock sector has recorded a 43pc increase in animal exports, with 400,000 animals prepared for export in a year and rural livestock farmers expected to earn Rs11 billion.

This was claimed by the government in a press release attributing the success to the Chief Minister’s Punjab Livestock Card Scheme launched by her under which farmers are receiving Rs27,000 per animal to meet feed and fodder expenses.
Under the Livestock Connect system, the government has established direct links with 1,725 fattening farms, 20 export slaughterhouses, 88 meat exporters and 34 meat traders.

stories.title: Tensions in Gulab Devi Lahore after patient’s death, brawl between attendants, doctors
summary: LAHORE: Tensions spiked in the Gulab Devi Hospital when a young male patient died soon after a physical clash between his female relatives and a lady doctor in the hospital.
Later, the male colleagues of the lady doctor claimed that she had turned towards one of the female attendants to stop her from recording her video.
They also lashed out at the police for use of excessive force for arresting and sending female attendants behind the bars at a time when their patient was in need of critical care.

stories.title: Questions raised over Islamabad's Pims doctors’ absorption process
summary: ISLAMABAD: Questions have been raised over the Ministry of Health’s handling of the absorption of doctors at the Pakistan Institute of Medical Sciences (Pims).

Doctors urge health ministry to implement SC judgement without discrimination “The ministry had proposed that such doctors should either be absorbed in Pims at the bottom of the existing seniority list or returned to their parent institutions,” he claimed.
Doctors have urged the ministry to implement the Supreme Court judgement transparently and without discrimination, particularly in the wake of the recent Pims fire tragedy.

stories.title: Bahawalpur CCD accused of kidnapping girl during raid
summary: BAHAWALPUR: Residents of Chak187/EB have accused plainclothes Crime Control Department (CCD) officials of illegally entering two homes and torturing women and children, and taking away a girl in a civilian vehicle during a raid to arrest a suspect.

According to details, the residents claimed that plainclothes personnel, without any lady police constable, entered two houses, maltreated women and children, and when the suspect they were looking for was not found, they allegedly took a girl along with them.

When contacted, Vehari Police spokesperson confirmed that a Burewala CCD team conducted a raid on a house in Chak 187/EB to arrest a wanted suspect named Bilal, who was nominated in a burglary case at Gaggo Mandi police station.

stories.title: Rawalpindi orders safety audit of 8,300 public, private schools
summary: Inspection teams to submit reports by Oct 20; private schools’ association seeks more time to prepare for security checks He said the teams began inspections on Sunday to cover all 7,000 private schools and 1,300 public-sector schools in the district.
The notification mandates an audit of security measures at public and private educational institutions.

The association has urged the deputy commissioner to revise the inspection schedule and allow institutions sufficient time to prepare for the audits, complete documentation and review their security arrangements.

stories.title: The data centre and water question
summary: AS plans for large data centres take shape in Pakistan, the debate has centred on jobs and investment, while a more basic concern has received little attention: water.

By 2030, the United Nations University projects that data centres globally will use nearly triple the combined electricity usage of Pakistan, Bangladesh and Nigeria, with an associated water footprint equal to the basic domestic needs of 1.3 billion people.
Hence, nationally, data centres are not Pakistan’s water problem.

The event also highlighted the importance of cooperation among public-sector institutions and healthcare professionals in strengthening emergency response systems, advancing medical training and promoting a culture of prevention throughout society.

stories.title: Patient, three attendants hurt as plaster of Larkana CMCH ward’s ceiling collapses
summary: LARKANA: A big chunk of the RCC plaster, along with a large portion of the false ceiling covering it, fell onto a patient and her attendants in a ward at the Chandka Medical College Teaching Hospital on Sunday.
The hospital staff and the victims’ relatives rushed them to the Larkana Trauma Centre for emergency treatment.
Advocate Abdul Hafeez Chawro, a relative of Pathani Khatoon, told media personnel that she had been admitted to the hospital and accommodated in the ward for the treatment of lung ailment.

stories.title: Persisting fault lines
summary: Recent events have deepened some of the country’s overlapping fault lines — enduring features that have shaped its political landscape for decades.
Government-opposition conflicts have been endemic in Pakistan’s history, with political behaviour driven by the ethic of war rather than competition.

While linked to government-opposition conflict, the second fault line is distinct: troubled relations and friction between the centre and provinces, which have punctuated the country’s history and weakened federalism.

stories.title: 20 booked for illegal hunting in Lahore
summary: LAHORE: During the ongoing operations of the Punjab Wildlife & Parks Department, 20 individuals involved in the illegal hunting and possession of falcons, doves, quails, hares and wild boars have been apprehended.
During these operations, a monkey and 16 wild birds were recovered, while several netting gears and hunting equipment were confiscated.
In another operation, Kasur wildlife rangers apprehended a hunter involved in the illegal netting of wild birds and imposed a fine of Rs20,000.

stories.title: LITERARY NOTES: Despite criticism, Hayaat-i-Javed and Sir Syed live on
summary: True to its name, Hayaat-i-Javed (1901), Sir Syed’s biography penned by Altaf Husain Hali, too, along with Sir Syed, has lived for over 125 years.

In addition to his research-based annotations, Badauni has written two prefaces and both are research papers unto themselves, sifting through the heaps of the material on Hali, Sir Syed and Hayaat-i-Javed.
Dr Badauni thinks Hayaat-i-Javed also serves as an intellectual history of the 19th-century Muslims in the subcontinent, as well as Sir Syed’s life and his achievements.

stories.title: Two moments of madness cost Sri Lanka as Pakistan win tri-series opener after Salman Ali Agha century
summary: Only 53 runs stood between them and a flying start in the One-day International tri-series opener against Pakistan after Pavan Rathnayake and Janith Liyanage’s 119-run stand.

Naseem Shah then had Sachindu Colombage caught behind, Eshan Malinga was run out after a mix-up, and Haris cleaned up Asitha Fernando to seal a 37-run win for Pakistan, who had earlier posted 305 thanks to Salman Ali Agha’s fourth ODI century.
But Sri Lanka’s two costly shots ultimately decided the opener, handing Pakistan a winning start to the tri-series.

stories.title: Gilgit-Baltistan CM vows transparent use of resources
summary: GILGIT: Gilgit-Baltistan Chief Minister Amjad Hussain has called for positive change in the region, pledging the effective and transparent use of resources that he said had not been properly utilised in the past.
The CM during his visit to Diamer held meetings with heads of government departments, met local residents and inspected development projects, hospitals, colleges and power projects.
The chief minister urged people to set aside their differences and work together for the region’s development.

stories.title: Agriculture: The growing threat of double-rice cropping
summary: Early rice cultivation has exposed a growing disconnect between the government’s regulatory framework and evolving cropping patterns.

Harvesting of the main (Kharif) rice crop is currently underway in Punjab, and field reports from the districts of Pakpattan, Okara and Sahiwal –areas known for double-rice cropping –indicate severe pest infestations, particularly by stem borers and top borers.

If the trend continues amid the current regulatory vacuum, Pakistan risks diminishing returns—using far more agricultural inputs while producing less rice overall – alongside severe financial losses for all rice farmers, whether or not they have adopted double-rice cropping.

Mr Khan emphasised that Chitral’s mining sector had significant untapped potential to stimulate economic growth, create employment opportunities and improve living standards in the impoverished region.

stories.title: Health directorate outlines plans to outsource hospitals in tribal districts
summary: PESHAWAR: The health directorate has outlined plans for the 12 designated districts including support for the ongoing process of outsourcing health facilities with enhanced monitoring to ensure that the residents of these areas get free diagnostic and medical services there.
Currently, 15 of the total 19 outsourced health facilities under public-private partnership (PPP) programme in merged districts will continue to operate owing to their better performance.

Official says enhanced monitoring to ensure residents of these areas get free diagnostic and medical services Health Foundation had planned to outsource 28 more hospitals in designated districts under public-private partnership mode.

stories.title: QWP blames PTI’s ‘non-serious attitude’ for govt loss
summary: Addressing a gathering at Watan Kor here the other day to mark the 14th foundation day of the QWP, Mr Sherpao held PTI leaders and its social media pressure groups responsible for the breakdown of talks with the federal government.
He alleged that the party had ignored the pressing issues confronting the province. “The PTI wasted precious time and resources of the province by staging useless long marches and protests,” he said.
Mr Sherpao said terrorism remained the biggest challenge facing the province, but alleged that the PTI leadership had failed to take effective measures to address the problem.

stories.title: Bhabara Bazaar offers a glimpse into Rawalpindi’s forgotten past
summary: Once an upscale locality of Rawalpindi under British rule, Bhabara Bazaar recalls the region’s majestic past in the heart of the garrison city.
Bhabara Bazaar is a two-kilometre-long residential and commercial locality built by the Bhabra community, belonging to Jainism, in the early 18th century.
The old residential streets of Bhabara Bazaar have winding, narrow lanes, houses with handcrafted wooden doors and corridors leading to enclosed courtyards within their outer walls.

stories.title: Banks’ mandatory property documents reduced to five for Apna Ghar scheme
summary: ISLAMABAD: The Ministry of Housing and Works on Sunday said the property documents required by banks under the Apna Ghar Programme had been reduced to five and standardised on the directives of Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif.
It said the number of mandatory documents required by banks under the housing finance scheme had been reduced to five.

An official of the Ministry of Housing said the standardised and simplified documentation requirements would allow people owning different types of properties and plots to obtain loans under the scheme.

stories.title: Rural areas of Islamabad get first-ever waste collection facility
summary: ISLAMABAD: The Capital Development Authority (CDA), through a Turkish company, has launched a project for cleanliness and garbage collection in the rural areas of Islamabad.
However, CDA had decided to engage the company in the rural areas (package II).
Therefore, the officials said, the company had been directed to start its operation in rural areas immediately without formal inauguration of the project. “A mega inauguration was planned.

stories.title: Farmers stage demos for higher wheat support price
summary: LAHORE: Small farmers across the country staged demos on Sunday, demanding “guaranteed” support prices, including Rs5,000 per maund price for wheat, and an immediate halt to corporate land grabbing and genetically modified (GM) crops.
In the demos, the participants voiced strong opposition to IMF and World Bank-backed economic policies that promote market deregulation and the weakening of public agricultural institutions.

Their key demands include immediate restoration of the Pakistan Agricultural Storage and Services Corporation (PASSCO) and a robust public procurement mechanism to shield growers from exploitation by powerful middlemen and market cartels.

stories.title: Land dispute between railways and KMC over road construction erupts into street fighting
summary: The dispute soon escalated into a physical scuffle, with the railway police taking the chief of KMC City Wardens to a police station.

The railways, a federal government enterprise, maintained that the road project encroaches on land belonging to the Karachi Circular Railway (KCR) and that the construction on its land was without authorisation.

The incident unfolded on Sunday afternoon when the railways police officials intervened at the construction site and stopped the work, prompting the chief of KMC City Wardens to arrive with their contingent.

stories.title: Cotton arrivals jump 7.5pc as textile crisis deepens
summary: Industry representatives have attributed the crisis to rising production costs and alleged misuse of the Export Facilitation Scheme (EFS), under which imported yarn and fabric are reportedly being sold in the domestic market instead of being re-exported.
According to the Pakistan Cotton Ginners Association (PCGA), arrivals reached 4,081,265 bales by Oct 15, up 285,628 bales from 3,795,637 bales a year earlier.
Mr Mahmood said the success of cotton revival should be measured by farmers’ net income per acre, not merely the volume of arrivals at ginning factories.

stories.title: 18 marble workers abducted in Khuzdar
summary: QUETTA: As many as 18 labourers working at a marble mine in the Naal area, about 40 kilometres from Khuzdar city, were kidnapped on Sunday, police said.
A large group of armed men entered the mine premises, held the labourers at gunpoint and abducted 18 of them, along with the son of a mine factory’s owner, officials said.
Officials said security forces had launched a search operation in the area to trace the abd­u­cted labourers.

stories.title: NCCIA arrests 1,129 suspects
summary: According to a one-month performance report after Director General Syed Ali Nasir Rizvi assumed charge, the agency received 5,176 complaints over the past month, on which 4,491 inquiries were registered.
Upon completion of inquiries, 272 cases were registered against those involved in cybercrime.
Mr Rizvi said that ensuring digital protection of people would be a priority and a zero-tolerance policy against cybercrime would continue to be strictly enforced.

stories.title: Gwadar port development projects reviewed
summary: GWADAR: A high-level meeting, presided over by Maritime Affairs Secretary Muhammad Khurram Agha, was held in Gwadar on Sunday to review progress on ongoing development projects in the port city.
The briefing covered Gwadar Port’s strategic importance, efforts to promote commercial activities and development of the free zone.
The plan is considered important for the future development of Gwadar Port and associated commercial and industrial activities.
